env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# The right-hand side of a property write that holds a brace literal ends
# at its last token: an address of a composite literal, a parenthesised
# one, and a method call on one. The module runs natively, ejects, and
# the ejected module builds and runs with go and with go1.27.2 from
# $UPROOT1272 and prints the same output.
cd m
logos run .
stdout '^5 6 7 8$'
cp stdout $WORK/native.txt
logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
exists $UPROOT1272/bin/go
exec $UPROOT1272/bin/go version
stdout '^go version go1\.27\.2 '
exec env -u GOROOT $UPROOT1272/bin/go build -o $WORK/upstream$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/upstream$GOEXE
cmp stdout $WORK/native.txt
exec $GOROOT/bin/gofmt -l .
! stdout .
cd ..

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/propbrace

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

type Item struct {
	N int
}

func (i Item) Ptr() *Item {
	return &Item{N: i.N + 1}
}

type Holder interface {
	Cur *Item
}

type Box struct : Holder {
	cur *Item
}

func (b *Box) Cur() *Item {
	return b.cur
}

func (b *Box) SetCur(v *Item) {
	b.cur = v
}

func main() {
	b := Box{cur: &Item{}}
	var h Holder = &b
	h.Cur = &Item{N: 5}
	first := h.Cur.N
	h.Cur = (&Item{N: 6}) // comment after a parenthesised literal
	second := h.Cur.N
	h.Cur = Item{N: 6}.Ptr() /* block comment after a call on a literal */
	third := h.Cur.N
	h.Cur = &Item{
		N: 8,
	}
	fmt.Println(first, second, third, h.Cur.N)
}
